content.intro: In this lesson, you will study asp development environment troubleshooting as part of Classic ASP development and legacy maintenance. The lesson follows the attached ASP curriculum topic 15 and uses the syllabus subtopics as the coverage checklist.
content.why_it_matters: ASP Development Environment Troubleshooting matters because Classic ASP behavior crosses a server-side scripting engine, IIS configuration, request/response boundaries, and often COM or ADO dependencies. A small, explicit test helps distinguish intended behavior from runtime-specific behavior.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: This topic connects HTTP and IIS configuration to the actual Classic ASP request path. The `.asp` extension alone does not guarantee execution: the relevant IIS feature, application mapping, site binding, physical path, permissions, and provider/runtime dependencies all matter. Diagnose one layer at a time and use a test site rather than changing production defaults blindly.

content_blocks.title: Syllabus coverage
content_blocks.text: The lesson explicitly covers: ASP pages downloading instead of executing; HTTP 404 errors; HTTP 403 errors; HTTP 500 errors; IIS configuration and permissions errors. Treat these subtopics as connected requirements. For each one, be able to define the concept, identify where it appears in a Classic ASP application, and name one test or diagnostic that would verify it.

content_blocks.limitations: Not executed during course generation. Classic ASP examples require a configured Windows/IIS environment with the matching ASP scripting engine and any required COM/ADO providers. Provider-specific and IIS-version-specific behavior must be verified locally.

content_blocks.title: Runtime and safety checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Run the example only on a local or test IIS site with the Classic ASP feature enabled. Record the OS, IIS version, site binding, physical directory, and the exact URL used. The source syllabus treats Classic ASP as a legacy maintenance technology, not as ASP.NET or a default choice for new web projects.

content_blocks.title: Guided workflow
content_blocks.text: 1. Start with a minimal local example of asp development environment troubleshooting. 2. Trace its inputs, state changes, dependencies, and output. 3. Test a normal case, a missing/malformed case, and one permission/provider/runtime failure. 4. Write down the exact expected and observed result before changing another variable.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating legacy runtime behavior as universal.
common_mistakes.why: IIS versions, Windows lifecycle, COM registration/bitness, and ADO providers can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Write down the actual server/provider versions and validate on a disposable test site.

common_mistakes.why: Empty input, missing records, expired sessions, permissions, timeouts, and malformed data reveal different failure modes.
common_mistakes.fix: Add normal, negative, and boundary cases with expected outcomes.

common_mistakes.why: Detailed errors can reveal paths, SQL text, configuration, and component information.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep diagnostics in restricted server-side logs and return a generic message with a reference ID.
